key_insight: GA-AMNO separates adaptive mesh neural operators into two inspectable parts: physics-informed allocation of computation and geometry-aware transport of features before aggregation.
engineering_relevance: This helps scientific ML models remain accurate and interpretable when PDE solvers change discretization, mesh density, or local geometry across domains.
method: Adaptive mesh selection decides where to compute based on local physics.
Gauge-aware low-rank transport maps source features into the target node's geometric context before message aggregation.
The framework includes conditions for representation-consistent aggregation and analyzes transport error under mesh deformation.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on five PDE benchmarks, with controlled interventions and geometric-mismatch tests showing better prediction accuracy and improved cross-discretization compatibility.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of topology-preserving mesh deformations and the stability of the low-rank transport approximation under strong geometric mismatch.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
